5.5. It is well settled that the proceedings before the Claims Tribunal are in the nature of inquiry.
In Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors [(2009) 13 SC 530, [in Sachin vs Shabuddin on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147889029/
6
Kaushnumma Begum and others V/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC [in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken.
From the stand of respondent no. 1 in his WS, it is clear that he is accepting the factum of accident but has disputed that he was rash or negligent in driving the offending bus and has rather claimed that driver of the said motorcycle suddenly turned his motorcycle, lost control over it and struck with the offending vehicle.
Thus, the factum of accident and the identity of respondent no. 1 Sabuddin as driver of the offending Cluster Bus bearing registration no. DL-1PD-1130, stands established.
In the cross- MACT No. 516/2023 Sachin Vs. Sabudin & Ors. page 13 of 32 examination, PW1 has admitted that he was driving motorcycle at the time of accident and they were three (persons sitting) on the motorcycle at the time of accident, which was a traffic violation & was possessing Learner's licence.
Merely because PW1 had admitted in the cross-examination that he had overtaken the offending bus from left side, it cannot be inferred that the driver of the offending bus bearing registration no.1 was not negligent as PW1 had categorically deposed that respondent no. 1 had suddenly took left turn without using any indication and as a result of sudden turn, his motorcycle engulfed with the offending vehicle.
Since the respondent no. 1 was driving a heavy vehicle i.e. bus and had a greater duty of care and turning the said bus suddenly without giving indicator to turn left, resulting into the accident and injuries to the three victims, was certainly negligent driving of the respondent no. 1.
From the same and on the basis of the site plan,
which is also the part of DAR Ex. PW1/A (colly), the principle of res ispa loquitur squarely applies to the facts of the present case qua rashness and negligence on the part of respondent no.1 (driver) in causing the said accident.
In this regard, reliance is also placed on the judgment in the case of State of Orissa Vs Nalini Kumar Patnaik, 1989 ACJ 126 Orissa.
Furthermore, in view of filing of DAR containing the charge-sheet for the offences u/s 279/337/338 IPC & other relevant documents against the respondent no. 1 and in terms of the judgment in the case of "National Insurance Co. Vs.
Pushpa Rana & Ors.", 2009 ACJ 287, Delhi, respondent no. 1 Sabuddin (driver of the offending vehicle) is held to be negligent on the basis of preponderance of probability.
From the DAR, it is also stands established that respondent no.2-Antony Road Transport Solution Pvt. Ltd. was the registered owner of the offending vehicle, which was insured with respondent no.3-IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd. vide Policy No. MS674328, valid from 21.01.2023 to midnight of 20.01.2024.
MACT No. 516/2023 Sachin Vs. Sabudin & Ors. page 16 of 32 5.8
As per the DAR Ex. PW1/A (colly) also, the driver namely Sachin (petitioner herein) of the motorcycle bearing no. DL- 5SCX-4423 was not possessing valid Licence at the time of accident and was triple riding the same and as such was challaned for the offences u/s 3/181 & u/s 194C M.V. Act and Smt. Sita Rani, owner of the said vehicle, who had given the said vehicle to the petitioner Sachin for driving the same, was also challaned u/s 5/180 of M.V. Act.
In such circumstances and by application of the principles of Preponderance of Probability, the petitioner Sachin Batham is held liable for contributory negligence and as such 25% (Twenty Five Percent)
shall be deducted from the amount, to be awarded as compensation to the petitioner, towards contributory negligence.
6.3.
Admittedly except the MLC of the petitioner which is part of DAR Ex. PW1/A (colly),
there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had taken any subsequent treatment qua the injuries sustained by him in the accident in question nor any document in this regard has been filed on record.
Considering the nature & extent of injuries suffered by the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the considered view that the petitioner/injured is not entitled to any compensation towards medical expenses.
7.5. As regards the attendant charges, petitioner/PW1 has not claimed any compensation under this head.
From the nature and extent of injuries suffered by the petitioner, it does not appear that he required any attendant.
Hence no compensation is awarded under the head of Nursing/Attendant Charges.
Admittedly there is no prescription advising the petitioner any special diet nor any such medical documents have been filed on record.
Considering the facts and circumstances and the MACT No. 516/2023 Sachin Vs. Sabudin & Ors. page 21 of 32 nature of the injury sustained by the petitioner
Considering the nature of injury of the petitioner and the fact that there is no document on record to show that the petitioner had taken any subsequent treatment or had visited the hospital for said purpose, no amount is awarded towards conveyance charges.
7.8. PW1/petitioner had claimed that due to injuries suffered in aforesaid accident, he suffered acute body pain for a month and could not resume his services for a month.
Keeping in view the fact that the petitioner suffered simple injury in the accident, he must have suffered some mental agony and pain due to the injury sustained by him,
therefore, a notional sum of Rs. 7,500/- is awarded to the petitioner under each head of "Loss due to Mental & Physical Shock" & "Pain & Suffering".
